notes:
This is a beta version, published only on the beta update channel. Warehouse and Day to day are finished and ready
to use: this version is here so that teams can start working with them now. It also brings the new RMM and end-user
features, which have not passed final verification yet and carry a visible Beta mark.

Before updating, make a backup and keep it (*Administration → System & updates → Backups*). This version changes
the database, and that backup is the safe way back (see *Keep in mind* at the end). A server on the stable channel is
not offered this version: to get it, choose the beta channel in *Administration → System & updates → Updates*.

What the Beta mark means: the feature works and you can use it as usual, but it has not passed final verification,
so some details may still change in a later version. The mark is only a notice: it doesn't limit anything or change
how the feature behaves, and it goes away when the feature passes. If something doesn't work as you expect, tell your
administrator. Anything without the mark is not in beta. The *Beta features* help article shows where the mark
appears.

Features marked Beta

- Agent policies: how endpoints are managed (patches, antivirus, agent updates, tray icon and alerts), with
  policies that inherit from each other and are assigned to endpoints, locations and companies. Updating creates two
  default policies, Windows and Linux, that do nothing automatically.
- Patches: the operating system and software patches missing on each endpoint; approve or reject them and install
  them in the policy's window or right away, with failures, restarts and alerts.
- Software and deployment: a software catalog to install or remove programs on endpoints by hand, in bulk or by
  policy.
- Uninstalling software: remove a program from an endpoint's inventory.
- Antivirus: which antivirus each endpoint has, whether it complies with the policy, its threats and actions.
- Antivirus consoles: connectors for SentinelOne, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and Sophos Central.
- Tray icon and help requests: the NetPilot icon in the Windows tray and Request help… with a screenshot.
- Agent auto-update: agents update themselves in the policy's window, with a pilot ring and automatic rollback.
- Full remote control: mouse, keyboard and clipboard on Windows endpoints, on top of the view-only mode of 1.8.2.
- Open sessions: the terminals, remote control, Remote Desktop and file transfers open right now, and how to close
  them.
- End users and their portal: give an employee access only to their devices, to turn them on and connect from the
  portal.
- Latest activity: a card in the endpoint's Summary with what last happened on it.
- Two-view history: Detail or Line in the change log and in the History tab of detail pages, except in
  Warehouse and Day to day.

New in Warehouse and Day to day

- Day to day, a section of its own: Today, Check lists, Briefs and Time tracking, with the Warehouse license.
- Check lists: lists with response types, templates, linked objects, team rounds, scheduling with a time window,
  Due now, signature, result, history and PDF.
- Report a problem, in Check lists and Today: for what breaks or goes missing outside a round, with a photo, site
  and object. It notifies whoever attends that site and, on a unit, whoever manages faults can open the fault.
- Deactivate a task of a list without deleting it, for seasonal work: it stops showing up in rounds and comes back
  when you activate it.
- Briefs: brief types, by hand or from a PDF with AI (also with Google Gemini), draft and publish, agenda, Live,
  My alerts and personal calendar.
- Time tracking: clocking in from Today, planned hours, special days, holidays, balance, Team records, CSV and
  monthly PDF.
- Warehouse: approval flows with up to 3 steps and a simulator, profiles, People and permissions, complete fault
  handling with repair shops, adding items with a photo, serial numbers from a photo, a bottom bar on mobile, an
  offline notice and installing it as an app.
- Request deletion: whoever can't delete an item or a unit requests it with a reason, from its page or from
  the lists. The request goes through the flows and approving it deletes nothing: afterwards, in To delete,
  someone with the permission chooses Delete or, if it has history, Archive (Write off for a unit).

What changes in Warehouse and Day to day

- Sections: whoever was limited to the Warehouse also gets Day to day. A simple menu for whoever only views,
  requests or approves. The bottom bar has Scan in the center.
- Permissions: importing needs *Import data*; categories, suppliers and bins,
  *Manage categories, suppliers and bins*; faults, *Report and manage faults, repairs and repair shops*; the wizard's
  initial stock needs *Register movements directly, without approval* as well as creating items. The built-in editor
  can now create categories and bins in their warehouses, and their permissions to manage check lists and briefs apply
  to the non-private ones in their scope. Warehouses are still for administrators.
  Everything that writes in the Warehouse, also through the AI Assistant, now respects the profile: an editor with
  a limited profile only does what the profile says (stock counts, minimums, installing and unlinking units, editing
  units, movements with the Assistant, attachments and journal of items, units and warehouses).
  Deleting a unit is no longer for administrators only: it needs *Delete items and units*.
- Catalog: a user limited by sites can create categories, suppliers and repair shops (categories and suppliers
  also when importing), but can't change or delete existing ones; one limited by company can't create them. Delete
  is only offered to whoever can do it.
- What applies to the whole organization: the Warehouse and briefs settings and the organization's brief types can
  only be changed by users without access limited to some sites or departments.
- Managers: they only give the editor role if they have it, and they don't manage their peers or anyone with more
  permissions. Changes to people ask you to confirm your identity.
- Flows: nobody approves their own request in a configured flow; approvers have to see the warehouse; users
  limited by sites can now request.
  A request without a warehouse is not handed out from a warehouse with its own flow: it has to be requested from
  that warehouse. A line without a cost no longer takes a request out of a minimum-amount flow. Cancel is for
  whoever requested, whoever can decide that step and administrators.
  Whoever requests a deletion doesn't decide it, not even in the default flow, and a deletion is only
  approved automatically in a flow that names that type.
- Requests: a serial-number item requested by quantity is handed out by choosing the units, and a loan of a
  quantity item goes out as an issue and comes back as a return. With access limited to some sites, a request made
  from any warehouse can now be decided and cancelled.
- Faults: they belong to units: a quantity item uses the *Damaged* or *Sent for repair* stock adjustment. There
  are new statuses and older faults keep theirs. When a fault is resolved, the unit goes back to its previous state. A
  return with damage opens the fault by itself.
- Check lists: existing tasks become Done / Not applicable; a new list is everyone's if whoever creates it can
  manage them, and private otherwise; starting joins you to the team round (of the open rounds from the previous
  version, the most recent of each list and site becomes the team round); a problem doesn't take the unit out of
  service and, on something that isn't a unit, notifies the person in charge or, on endpoints and devices, lets you
  create a ticket; a window nobody did stays as not done; sending a mark or a problem again after losing the response
  doesn't duplicate it. The expected code of a scan task no longer reaches whoever does the round.
- Briefs: existing ones move to the Club / audiovisual type, and their color and tech rider points move to "Other"
  (they are now day fields). Imported ones stay as drafts; a new brief is everyone's if whoever creates it can manage
  them, and private otherwise; a private brief isn't visible even to an administrator. Reading a PDF with the
  organization's AI key needs the permission to manage briefs (with your own key, access to Briefs is enough).
  Sharing a brief for editing doesn't let you change its site or department. The old way of uploading a PDF leaves
  a draft: it no longer publishes or notifies anyone. People in charge read by the AI are only linked if they are in
  your directory.
- Live: each DJ shows their visual or the day's general one; Next and After that carry visual, detail and
  colors; the prepare cards say the time; Correct opens the day in the editor.
- Brief alerts: they always appear inside NetPilot while it is open and, with permission, also as a notification.
  They say what it is and the time of the point.
- Rider notice: it says which party it is about and what changes, also in Today, and covers today and the next 7
  days.
- Calendar: events carry visual, colors and party; the double sunset alarm is gone.
- Rounds: To start says when and who did the last one; tapping a task with a required photo opens the camera on
  mobile; the round says who started it; "too fast" shows the time from first to last mark; Finish says which
  optional tasks are left.
- Hours: your own changes have a deadline and a limit of hours; deleting asks for a reason; the planned hours sent
  through the API when clocking in are ignored, they always come from the server; personal notices no longer go out
  through the organization's channels.
- Days in local time: filters, 30-day activity and what is overdue use the site's time zone.
- Mobile: the Assistant button and the notices appear above the bottom bar.

Keep in mind

- Agents: the Beta features that run on the endpoint need the new agent. Agents from 1.8.2 or earlier are moved
  once from *RMM → Agents* with Move to 1.9: despite its name, that button installs this server's version (1.8.3).
  From then on they update themselves.
- Going back from this version: if the database is downgraded, private lists and briefs and drafts can be seen by
  anyone with the view permission, and they are not deleted. What the previous version doesn't understand is lost:
  shifts deleted with a reason, pending rounds, cleared marks, problems reported without a round and whatever lives in
  new tables, such as holidays. Deactivated tasks end up removed from their list.
- Serial numbers without AI: the barcodes on the label are read, also on iPhone; printed text has to be typed.
- Offline cache: it is renewed on the first visit after updating.
- Manual: the PDF manual is still the 1.8 edition; the in-app help already covers everything new.
